what: The card runs as one stock Mastra workflow whose three steps each start the stage program as its own process
why: Each stage already has its own harness and store, and Mastra's observability database takes a process-wide lock; running the stages in one process would make the review and the builder fight for the writer
evidence: machine/parent/workflow.mjs starts build, remediation and landing through machine/parent/stages.mjs; machine/run.test.mjs runs the real entry point with stub programs and reads three succeeded stages in order

what: The run record is one JSON file per run under /var/lib/julia-dashboard/state/machine-runs/
why: A run is read as a whole, so one file needs no join and no schema migration, and the dashboard already reads that state folder
evidence: MACHINE_RUNS_DIR is honoured by both sides; a served dashboard listed a seeded record and its detail page
result: machine/parent/store.mjs writes atomically with a temporary file and a rename

what: Stalled is derived when the record is read, never stored
why: Storing it would need a second writer to notice a dead process, and a dead process cannot write; the reader has the clock
evidence: shownStatus returns running until heartbeatAt is older than the record's own idleLimitMs; a served run with a two-hour-old heartbeat showed a stalled pill
result: machine/parent/store.mjs, dashboard/lib/machine-runs.js, tested on both sides

what: The idle limit travels inside the record instead of being a constant in each reader
why: Two copies of ten minutes would drift, and the page would then disagree with the machine about the same run
evidence: record.idleLimitMs is written at run start from MACHINE_IDLE_LIMIT_MIN; dashboard/lib/machine-runs.js reads it from the record
result: machine/parent/store.test.mjs covers the fallback and the env override

what: The run writes a heartbeat every thirty seconds, and the stages are spawned asynchronously
why: spawnSync would block the event loop and stop the heartbeat, so a thirty-minute build would read as stalled
evidence: runStage resolves on the child's close event; machine/run.mjs keeps a 30s interval that rewrites heartbeatAt
result: the run test that fails at remediation still shows the record's later stages pending

what: The pull request names JUL-329, the card this session bills to
why: The scorecard prices a card from the sessions its own kickoff named, and this session was started for JUL-329; a slice's own PR can name the slice only when a session was kicked off naming that slice
evidence: docs/scorecards/JUL-330.md would print Cost: unknown; docs/scorecards/JUL-329.md prints a measured cost, and node scripts/check-branch-pr.mjs passed repository-hygiene on PR #433
result: recorded in the PR body's Deviation section

what: The runs pages are force-dynamic and carry no meta refresh
why: A meta refresh in the body is not valid in the app router, and a dynamic page recomputes on every request, which is what "a new run appears within one minute" needs
evidence: curl against the served dashboard returned the new run without a restart after the record file changed

what: scripts/start-machine.mjs is deleted in the same change that replaces it
why: A second entry point would keep its own state file and drift from the run records
evidence: grep over the repository finds no live reference; the old test file was removed with it
result: machine/run.mjs and machine/parent/README.md carry the entry point
